scenarios.title: Concurrent
scenarios.description: Two branches execute in parallel — the scheduler interleaves steps from each branch on every tick.

scenarios.title: Delay (decorator)
scenarios.description: Delay in decorator form pauses AFTER the step completes. Compare with standalone delay which is its own step between actions.

scenarios.title: Delay
scenarios.description: A virtual-time delay pauses the queue — the clock advances but no steps execute during the gap.

scenarios.title: Loop (until)
scenarios.description: Loop with count and until condition. Repeats up to N times or until the condition is met. Button "A" loops 3 times, button "B" loops until "true" (runs once).

scenarios.title: Loop
scenarios.description: The loop decorator repeats a step N times before advancing.

scenarios.title: Retry
scenarios.description: Retry decorator re-executes a step on failure up to N times. If the executor throws, the scheduler retries before advancing or failing the queue.

scenarios.title: Sequential
scenarios.description: Steps execute one after another in declaration order.

scenarios.title: Timeout
scenarios.description: Timeout decorator sets a maximum duration for a step. If the step takes longer, it is aborted.

scenarios.title: When Guard
scenarios.description: The when decorator conditionally skips a step based on a guard expression. B executes (when: true), C is skipped (when: false).

scenarios.title: Barrier
scenarios.description: N-way sync point. Three branches with staggered delays converge at a barrier — fast and medium block until slow arrives, then all proceed.

scenarios.title: Channel (via Signal)
scenarios.description: Two-way handshake. Producer signals data-ready, consumer processes and acks — round-trip coordination using signal pairs.

scenarios.title: Mutex
scenarios.description: Mutual exclusion via decorator. Steps tagged with the same mutex never run simultaneously across branches.

scenarios.title: Signal / Await
scenarios.description: One-way dependency between branches. Sender signals after a click, receiver blocks until the signal arrives.

scenarios.title: Accumulator
scenarios.description: Reduce-style aggregation — feeds values through a binary operator (sum, product, min, max). The accumulator starts at an identity value and applies the operator for each accumulate call.

scenarios.title: Counter
scenarios.description: Atomic counter — increment, decrement, add, and read. Each named counter is a singleton within the scope, so multiple steps share the same state.

scenarios.title: Flag
scenarios.description: Atomic boolean flag — set, clear, toggle, and check. Useful for signalling state changes between steps without passing data.

scenarios.title: Gauge
scenarios.description: Typed value holder with atomic compare-and-set. Unlike a counter, a gauge holds any value — use it for temperatures, levels, thresholds.

scenarios.title: Latch
scenarios.description: Countdown latch — starts at N, each countDown() decrements by 1. When count reaches zero, all waiters are released. Unlike a barrier, a latch is one-shot: once tripped it stays open.

scenarios.title: State Machine
scenarios.description: Declarative state machine with transitions, guards, and lifecycle handlers. Define states and allowed transitions, then drive the machine through its lifecycle.

scenarios.title: Channel
scenarios.description: Producer-consumer pattern — a bounded channel with capacity 2 connects a producer that sends 4 items to a consumer that receives them. The producer blocks when the channel is full until the consumer drains it.

scenarios.title: Combined Pipeline
scenarios.description: Rate-limited pipeline with deadline — composes semaphore, channel, spawned task, concurrent map, and deadline into a single workflow. A producer feeds items through a bounded channel, rate-limited workers process them under a semaphore gate, results accumulate in a concurrent map, and a deadline scopes the entire pipeline.

scenarios.title: Concurrent Map
scenarios.description: Concurrent map with atomic operations — parallel workers write to a shared map using put, putIfAbsent, merge, and computeIfAbsent. Each operation is atomic, preventing data races.

scenarios.title: Correlation Scope
scenarios.description: Async request/response correlation — register expected responses by key on a channel, send messages to the channel, then await correlated responses. The scope routes incoming messages by extracted key.

scenarios.title: Deadline Context
scenarios.description: Scoped deadline with cancellation — create a child scope with a deadline, run steps within it, and observe deadline expiry. The deadline fires a callback and marks remaining time as expired.

scenarios.title: Semaphore
scenarios.description: Rate-limited parallel workers — a semaphore with 2 permits gates 4 parallel tasks. Each worker acquires a permit before proceeding, blocking when none are available. Watch the trace to see only 2 workers active at a time.

scenarios.title: Spawned Task
scenarios.description: Background task lifecycle — spawn a long-running task, do other work in the foreground, then join the background task. Shows isDone/isFailed polling and join with timeout.

scenarios.title: Data Trigger
scenarios.description: External data activates a suspended queue. Main steps run first; the trigger queue waits until data arrives on the channel. Click Send to inject data.

scenarios.title: ForEach
scenarios.description: forEach stamps a template for each item in a list. One page definition expands to three region-specific dashboards with scoped ${each.*} variables.

scenarios.title: Modules
scenarios.description: Reusable modules with typed parameters and outputs. One module, three imports — each stamped with its alias. Outputs chain between modules via ${module.alias.output}.

scenarios.title: Orchestration Block
scenarios.description: Top-level orchestration block pre-declares barriers and signals. Init delays then signals, worker awaits, both sync at a barrier before proceeding.

scenarios.title: Time Trigger
scenarios.description: Time-based activation. A suspended queue activates after virtual time elapses. The main branch continues while the timer counts down.

scenarios.title: GraphQL Operation
scenarios.description: The graphql delivery type executes a domain operation via GraphQL. The domain and operation name route to a server-side resolver; params pass as variables.

scenarios.title: Mixed Delivery
scenarios.description: Scenarios can mix delivery types. Simulated steps inject data while ARIA steps interact with UI — they compose naturally in concurrent branches.

scenarios.title: Simulated Data
scenarios.description: The simulated delivery type injects data directly into a named dataset without any server call. Use it to pre-populate tables and charts in demos.

scenarios.title: Agent
scenarios.description: Agent binding — delegate work to an AI agent. The mock executor simulates dispatching a summarisation task and a code-generation task, returning structured output.

scenarios.title: GraphQL
scenarios.description: GraphQL binding — execute a query or mutation against a GraphQL endpoint. The mock executor simulates a users query and a createUser mutation with realistic response shapes.

scenarios.title: MCP
scenarios.description: MCP binding — invoke a Model Context Protocol tool. The mock executor simulates calling a file_search tool and a code_review tool, returning structured results.

scenarios.title: Process
scenarios.description: Process binding — execute an OS process. The mock executor simulates running ls and git status commands, capturing stdout and exit codes.

scenarios.title: REST
scenarios.description: REST binding — invoke an HTTP endpoint. Supports GET, POST, PUT, DELETE with headers and body. The mock executor simulates a GET request to a users API and a POST to create an order.

scenarios.title: Script
scenarios.description: Script binding — execute an inline script in a specified runtime (python3, node). The mock executor simulates running a Python data-processing script and a Node.js validation script.

scenarios.title: Barrier
scenarios.description: A barrier blocks until all named steps have completed. Use it to express "wait for A and B before proceeding."

scenarios.title: Block (sequential)
scenarios.description: A block groups steps that execute sequentially. Each step runs only after the previous one succeeds.

scenarios.title: If / Else
scenarios.description: Conditional branching — evaluates a condition, runs then-steps if truthy, else-steps otherwise. Conditions use the truthiness evaluator.

scenarios.title: Match / Cases
scenarios.description: Pattern matching with value, structural, any-of, and default patterns. The first matching case executes; later cases are skipped.

scenarios.title: Parallel
scenarios.description: Parallel runs multiple steps concurrently. All branches execute simultaneously — the step completes when all branches finish.

scenarios.title: Quorum
scenarios.description: Quorum succeeds when N of M named steps have completed — does not require all. Use for "any 2 of 3" patterns.

scenarios.title: Select (first-to-complete)
scenarios.description: Select races multiple branches — the first to complete wins. Wait branches block on named signals; the first signal to fire determines which branch executes.

scenarios.title: Try / Catch / Finally
scenarios.description: Structured error handling. Try-steps execute first; if any fails, catch-steps run. Finally-steps always execute regardless of outcome.
